packet.headline_seed: Dozens injured and thousands evacuated in Croatia wildfire
packet.description_seed: Officials say the blaze, near the port town of Omis, is one of the worst in Croatia's history.

what: Dozens injured and thousands evacuated in Croatia wildfire

clean_source_blocks.text: At least one person has died and around 40 others have been injured after a severe wildfire tore through cities on Croatia's coastline on Thursday night and Friday morning. The blaze broke out near the village of Lokva Rogoznica on Thursday evening, and spread quickly towards the nearby tourist town of Omis, 6km (7 miles) away. Around 1,200 residents and tourists were evacuated, while 10 people were in intensive care in hospital, the prime minister said. Croatia's fire chief Slavko Tucakovic described it as "one of the worst" blazes in the country's history. Croatia is one of several European nations suffering devastating wildfires, after a summer of extreme heat and dry conditions. Villages near the Adriatic city of Split were struck by the blaze, which coursed through pine forest-lined hillside, causing extensive damage to homes and cars.

Tucakovic said the firestorm burned through "everything in their path" as officials confirmed flames, fanned by strong winds, engulfed 1,000 hectares in just four hours. More than 300 firefighters were deployed overnight on Thursday, with crews sometimes forced to retreat as the fire advanced. Footage shared online shows thick smoke and huge flames tearing through surrounding vegetation, turning the sky red, as stranded residents and tourists looked on. Some people were forced to jump into the sea from boats to escape the fire. The wildfire has been described as "one of the worst" in the Croatia's history Emergency shelters were opened in several towns along the coast, as evacuations continued throughout the night. On Friday, officials confirmed that a body had been discovered in a burnt-out area as emergency services continued searching affected zones.
Officials say the blaze, near the port town of Omis, is one of the worst in Croatia's history.

A total of 157 firefighters and 44 fire engines were deployed to Lokva Rogoznica - a coastal village 23 miles south of Split - as video footage showed monstrous red flames engulfing the area, destroying several homes and cars. A catastrophic fire swept through Omis, Croatia on Thursday night, forcing 2,000 people to evacuate. Credit: AP Witnesses told Croatian broadcaster HRT that people were jumping into the sea after boats also caught fire. Evacuees, most of whom are foreign tourists, sought refuge at local sports centres. Altogether, 36 people from Omis received medical care. Residents and tourists evacuated from the Croatia wildfire gathered in a sports hall in Omis on Friday morning. Credit: AP British tourist Maxine Jones described on Facebook how she and her family fled to Split and slept on a hotel floor.

The wildfire has been described as "one of the worst" in the Croatia's history

Emergency shelters were opened in several towns along the coast, as evacuations continued throughout the night.

On Friday, officials confirmed that a body had been discovered in a burnt-out area as emergency services continued searching affected zones.

Later on Friday, Croatian Prime Minister Andrej Plenkovic visited the affected area, where he praised the work of emergency crews.

The fire had spread at "lightning speed" and with "gale-force winds", he told reporters, adding that what firefighters had managed to save was "truly a miracle".

The Commander of Omis Volunteer Fire Department, Viseslav Pesic told Reuters the blaze was so intense that people had abandoned vehicles "directly in the fire zone", making it difficult for emergency crews to pass through.

Huge red flames engulfed the Croatian coastal village of Lokva Rogoznica as Europe continues to battle wildfires. ITV News Correspondent John Ray reports

Firefighters continued to tackle wildfires across Europe on Friday as record-breaking heat gripped the continent.

Thousands have been forced to evacuate their homes, several of which have been destroyed, as hundreds of firefighters worked to tackle multiple blazes.

A mix of strong winds, hot temperatures and lack of rainfall has fuelled the flames, hindering extinguishing efforts.

ITV News looks at which areas have been impacted.

One person died and 14 were hospitalised from a fire that raged by the coastal town of Omis on Thursday night.

Seven people remained in a life-threatening condition early Friday and at least 2,000 people were forced to evacuate their homes.

A total of 157 firefighters and 44 fire engines were deployed to Lokva Rogoznica - a coastal village 23 miles south of Split - as video footage showed monstrous red flames engulfing the area, destroying several homes and cars.

A catastrophic fire swept through Omis, Croatia on Thursday night, forcing 2,000 people to evacuate. Credit: AP

Witnesses told Croatian broadcaster HRT that people were jumping into the sea after boats also caught fire.

Evacuees, most of whom are foreign tourists, sought refuge at local sports centres. Altogether, 36 people from Omis received medical care.

Residents and tourists evacuated from the Croatia wildfire gathered in a sports hall in Omis on Friday morning. Credit: AP

British tourist Maxine Jones described on Facebook how she and her family fled to Split and slept on a hotel floor.

"We managed to escape last night [Thursday] and drove to Split. We found a hotel that is fully booked but they allowed us four adults and our two grandchildren to stay on their conference room floor. They have been extremely kind," she said.

Firefighters put out the blaze by Friday morning as other crews in planes headed further south toward the Peljesac peninsula where another wildfire broke out overnight.

Chief Fire Chief Slavko Tucaković told Croatian newspaper Jutarnji list he had never experienced such a fire in his life. He also said burning vehicles may have contributed to the spread of the fire.
